# **ResolventKV: Subspace Resolvent Causal Closure for Recomputation-Free Composable LLM State**

## **1\. Verdict and Candidate Selection**

The selected foundational technology bears the working name **ResolventKV** (Subspace Resolvent Causal Closure for Position-Independent KV State), classified under the deep-tech taxonomy as a **Potentially Novel Mechanism** that synthesizes a **Novel Combination** of spiked-covariance optimal singular value shrinkage1, exact log-partition softmax stitching, and block-lower-triangular Neumann resolvent perturbation propagation2 to satisfy the non-prefix causal-closure contract5. Its central technical insight is that by projecting independently precomputed Key-Value (KV) chunks onto their low-rank spiked spectral subspaces and solving inter-chunk causal conditioning via a block-lower-triangular Neumann resolvent sweep over exact FlashAttention log-normalizers, an inference engine can assemble arbitrary out-of-order context blocks in ![][image1] time—restoring full-prefill multi-hop equivalence at less than ![][image2] of token-level prefill FLOPs without re-encoding token suffixes or fine-tuning model weights \[Hypothesis\].  
In plain English, modern AI applications—such as autonomous coding agents, tool-using workflows, and multi-document retrieval systems—repeatedly feed the same documents, skills, and memory blocks into large language models (LLMs), but in different orders and positions on every turn6 \[Verified Fact\]. Current production caches only work when shared text appears in the exact same order at the very beginning of a prompt7 \[Verified Fact\]. When a document shifts position or appears after another dynamically inserted document, the serving engine must either recompute the heavy neural network layers from scratch or paste together isolated caches that never interacted with one another, causing severe accuracy drops on multi-document reasoning tasks5 \[Verified Fact\]. ResolventKV overcomes this bottleneck by storing a compact mathematical summary—capturing the dominant spectral directions and attention normalizers—alongside each cached text block \[Hypothesis\]. When blocks are combined in a novel order at runtime, ResolventKV solves a lightweight matrix equation across those compact summaries to calculate how earlier blocks mathematically shift the attention states of later blocks, updating the cached representations in place within milliseconds without running the full language model over the text again \[Hypothesis\].

## **2\. Why Now: Converging Evidence and Structural Trends**

Five empirical developments between early 2025 and October 2026 have converged to expose both an acute infrastructure bottleneck in production LLM serving and the mathematical levers required to resolve it. First, exact-prefix caching—the foundational prefill optimization in vLLM's PagedAttention22 and SGLang's RadixAttention7—has suffered a structural breakdown under agentic workloads \[Verified Fact\]. Prefix caching assumes that turn ![][image14] is a strict append-only continuation of turn ![][image15] starting from token index ![][image16], enabling the engine to hash token sequences sequentially7 \[Verified Fact\]. However, agentic orchestration frameworks (such as OpenClaw, LangGraph, and tool-using coding agents) dynamically assemble prompts every turn by interleaving static system instructions, evolving histories, re-ranked retrieval chunks, and compacted tool outputs7 \[Verified Fact\]. This composition shifts bit-identical token spans to new absolute positions7 \[Verified Fact\]. Workload telemetry published in May 2026 demonstrates that up to ![][image17] of session tokens (at the 95th percentile within-session on the Toolathlon benchmark) repeat at shifted positions7 \[Verified Fact\]. Production OpenClaw operator post-mortems document that retrieval re-ranking, forward-iterating compaction past the ![][image18] context threshold, and process-spawning regressions routinely strand ![][image19] to ![][image20] token histories outside the prefix cache, collapsing cache hit rates from ![][image21] down to ![][image22] or ![][image23] and inducing Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) spikes of ![][image24] to ![][image25] seconds on unchanged content7 \[Verified Fact\].  
Second, the October 2026 publication of **SAFE-KV** exposed a severe causal-closure wall in Position-Independent Caching (PIC)5 \[Verified Fact\]. While early PIC systems assumed that encoding chunks independently and applying a relative rotary position (![][image3]\-RoPE) shift at lookup would suffice, SAFE-KV proved that a cached document state is a context-conditioned causal state whose keys and values depend on the preceding documents present when it was encoded12 \[Verified Fact\]. Even under prefix-conditioned composition—where every document ![][image26] is encoded under the exact static chat prefix ![][image27] and at its target global position to eliminate both prefix and position mismatch—reusing composed caches on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct preserves only ![][image28] of full-prefill answers on HotpotQA-500 and ![][image29] on 2WikiMultihopQA-5005 \[Verified Fact\]. Because causal self-attention is transitive, every slice ![][image30] with ![][image31] in a composed cache was computed under a history omitting document ![][image32]; consequently, repairing only the selected high-risk document ![][image32] on 2Wiki-100 lifts answer preservation from ![][image33] to merely ![][image34]5 \[Verified Fact\]. To achieve causal closure, SAFE-KV must re-encode the entire contiguous document suffix ![][image35], which recovers ![][image36] to ![][image37] equivalence on HotpotQA-500 and ![][image38] on 2Wiki-500, but forces the engine to re-encode ![][image39] and ![][image40] of the entire prompt context at the K2 operating point5 \[Verified Fact\]. Because faithful suffix repair re-encodes nearly the entire prompt, SAFE-KV's latency-gated operating rule on a single-request NVIDIA L40S testbed serves every workload by falling back to ![][image21] full prefill5 \[Verified Fact\].  
![][image41]  
Third, controlled mechanistic studies in September 2026 (**ATTUNER**) localized the root cause of PIC quality degradation to attention routing rather than value degradation6 \[Verified Fact\]. Evaluating Qwen3-4B across SRA-Bench, MuSiQue, and PersonaMem-v2, the ATTUNER study separated *artifact discovery* (selecting relevant blocks among distractors) from *evidence utilization* (reading and integrating multi-artifact content)6 \[Verified Fact\]. The authors proved that independently cached blocks retain faithful internal value representations, and that constructing an **attention routing oracle**—which replaces PIC's attention score distribution with full-prefill attention scores while leaving the cached KV tensors completely untouched—recovers full-prefill accuracy24 \[Verified Fact\]. This finding establishes that cross-chunk causal errors stem primarily from uncalibrated attention partition functions and routing drift across chunks \[Technical Inference\].  
Fourth, spectral analyses in April and May 2026 proved that KV caches possess low-rank spiked structure along the token dimension. In April 2026, **eOptShrinkQ** demonstrated that an ![][image42] block of consecutive key or value vectors ![][image43] is not a collection of independent vectors, but follows a spiked random matrix model ![][image44] with a low-rank shared signal ![][image45] of effective rank ![][image46] whose singular values exceed the Baik-Ben Arous-Péché (BBP) phase transition threshold ![][image47], alongside a separable noise residual ![][image48]1 \[Verified Fact\]. In May 2026, **CacheTune** independently confirmed that token-dimension KV energy is heavily concentrated in low-frequency spectral components, and that those low-frequency modes govern inter-chunk cross-attention restoration29 \[Verified Fact\].  
Fifth, **CoMem** and **EncBank** (October 2026\) established that pretrained decoders naturally split at an intermediate layer boundary ![][image49] (such as ![][image50] on Qwen3-8B), where lower layers ![][image51] act as a local document encoder—exhibiting the block-diagonal intra-passage attention sparsity documented by Meta's **REFRAG**30—while upper layers ![][image52] perform cross-chunk integration32 \[Verified Fact\]. Complementing this, **SpecCache** (ACL July 2026\) proved that deep-layer representations are far more sensitive to cross-chunk KV deviations than the shallow layer-1 features relied upon by earlier systems like CacheBlend34 \[Verified Fact\]. Together, these five findings imply that causal suffix closure only needs to be solved in the upper layers, and can be executed over a low-rank spectral basis rather than full token sequences \[Hypothesis\].

## **3\. Technical Hypothesis: Breaking the Token-Domain Causal Assumption**

### **Established Science: Causal Self-Attention and Non-Prefix Discrepancies**

In a standard decoder-only Transformer with ![][image53] layers and hidden dimension ![][image54], processing a concatenated sequence of context blocks ![][image55]—where ![][image56] is a static system prefix, ![][image57] are retrieved documents or agentic memory/tool artifacts of token length ![][image58], and ![][image59] is the active user query—requires computing causal self-attention at every layer ![][image60]24 \[Verified Fact\]. For any token position ![][image61] inside block ![][image57], the pre-projection attention output ![][image62] within an attention head is governed by the partitioned softmax equation35 \[Verified Fact\]:  
![][image63]  
When blocks are precomputed independently under the static prefix ![][image56] (the prefix-conditioned baseline formalized in SAFE-KV5), the middle summation over preceding chunks ![][image64] is absent during cache generation \[Verified Fact\]. Each block ![][image57] therefore stores isolated key-value tensors ![][image65] projected from isolated residual states ![][image66]5 \[Verified Fact\].  
When ![][image67] are dynamically composed at inference time, two mathematical discrepancies separate the composed cache ![][image68] from the full-prefill cache ![][image69]5 \[Verified Fact\]. The first discrepancy is positional offset (![][image70]): chunk ![][image57] now sits at global coordinate ![][image71] rather than its encoding offset ![][image72]7 \[Verified Fact\]. Because Rotary Position Embeddings (RoPE) apply an orthogonal block-diagonal rotation ![][image73], this offset is algebraically invertible and correctable in closed form via ![][image74] across the full key dimension ![][image75] in Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) or across the ![][image76]\-dimensional RoPE key slice ![][image77] (![][image78] of the KV row) in Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), where ![][image3]\-rotation introduces a bounded relative ![][image79] error of only ![][image80] in bfloat167 \[Verified Fact\]. The second, far harder discrepancy is missing cross-chunk causal history (![][image81]): because token ![][image82] never attended to ![][image83] at layer ![][image84], its attention output ![][image85] omits cross-chunk value contributions and cross-chunk softmax denominator mass, perturbing its residual state ![][image86] and recursively shifting the keys and values ![][image87] and ![][image88] at all deeper layers ![][image89] and across all downstream chunks ![][image90]5 \[Verified Fact\].

### **The Hidden Assumption in Current Systems**

Every existing non-prefix KV cache reuse architecture operates under an unexamined assumption: **that propagating the cross-chunk causal perturbation ![][image91] across a sequence of composed chunks requires either executing the Transformer's token-level layers online or training auxiliary neural network weights per model checkpoint** \[Technical Inference\].  
Online token-recomputation systems—including CacheBlend11, EPIC25, ProphetKV40, SpecCache34, CacheTune29, and SAFE-KV5—assume that repairing cached KV states requires selecting a subset of tokens or document spans and passing them through the full ![][image92] attention projections and ![][image93] feed-forward networks at every layer \[Verified Fact\]. As SAFE-KV and recent request-history sensitivity studies demonstrated, scattered token updates suffer from high answer variance across rolling request histories25 and violate causal closure whenever unrepaired tokens follow repaired tokens5, whereas contiguous suffix recomputation forces the engine to re-encode over ![][image94] of the prompt, negating the latency advantage of caching5 \[Verified Fact\]. Conversely, training-based adaptation systems—including KV Packet39, ATTUNER6, C2KV42, CacheRepair44, and EncBank32—avoid online token recomputation by training soft-token boundary wrappers, query-side LoRA adapters, sidecar extractors, or residual repair networks via self-distillation \[Verified Fact\]. However, training-based methods require offline optimization pipelines for every model checkpoint, break zero-shot compatibility across multi-LoRA agent fleets45, and—when cached chunk KV states are held strictly static as in KV Packet and ATTUNER—prevent an intermediate chunk ![][image95] from updating its internal keys to relay multi-hop entity bindings from ![][image96] to ![][image97]24 \[Technical Inference\].

### **The Proposed Mechanism: ResolventKV**

ResolventKV eliminates both online token-level FFN execution and offline adapter training by reformulating inter-chunk causal closure as a **low-rank spectral boundary-value problem** solved analytically during cache assembly \[Hypothesis\]. The mechanism combines three mathematical pillars.

#### **Pillar 1: Exact Log-Partition Softmax Stitching Within Each Layer**

During the initial offline encoding of chunk ![][image57] (conditioned on the canonical sink prefix ![][image98]), standard FlashAttention-2 and FlashMLA kernels compute not only the isolated attention output ![][image99] and un-rotated KV states ![][image100], but also the exact per-token log-sum-exp normalizer ![][image101], where ![][image102] is the partition function of the intra-chunk softmax7 \[Verified Fact\]. When chunk ![][image57] is placed after preceding chunks ![][image83], the exact attention output of token ![][image82] (prior to upstream KV perturbations) is a convex combination of its isolated attention output and its cross-chunk attention output ![][image103] over ![][image83] \[Technical Inference\]:  
![][image104]  
Here, ![][image105] is the logistic sigmoid of the log-normalizer difference \[Technical Inference\]. This formulation naturally exploits the block-diagonal attention sparsity observed by REFRAG30: whenever chunk ![][image57] has low semantic affinity with ![][image83], ![][image106], driving ![][image107] and leaving the isolated representation undisturbed \[Technical Inference\].

#### **Pillar 2: Spiked-Subspace Reduction and Frechet Susceptibility**

Evaluating ![][image108] and ![][image103] across all token pairs ![][image109] would still incur ![][image110] complexity, and propagating the resulting residual perturbation ![][image91] through the non-linear SwiGLU FFN at every token would still incur ![][image111] complexity36 \[Verified Fact\]. However, by **eOptShrinkQ**'s spiked covariance theorem1 and **CacheTune**'s spectral energy theorem29, the token-dimension variation of keys, values, and attention perturbations within chunk ![][image57] is governed by a low-rank subspace of dimension ![][image112] (such as ![][image113] for ![][image114], a ![][image115] sequence reduction) \[Verified Fact\]. During the offline write of chunk ![][image57], ResolventKV applies optimal singular value shrinkage (eOptShrink1) to extract an orthonormal temporal basis ![][image116], projects the chunk's queries, keys, values, and log-normalizers onto ![][image117] to form rank\-![][image118] spectral centroids ![][image119], and evaluates a low-rank factored **Frechet Susceptibility Operator** ![][image120] via a batched Jacobian-vector product (JVP) over the ![][image118] basis modes \[Hypothesis\]. This susceptibility operator maps a rank\-![][image118] attention shift ![][image121] at layer ![][image84] directly to the induced rank\-![][image118] shift in next-layer keys and values ![][image122] without executing token-level FFNs at runtime \[Hypothesis\].

#### **Pillar 3: Block-Lower-Triangular Neumann Resolvent Causal Closure**

ResolventKV combines Pillars 1 and 2 with **CoMem/EncBank**'s depth split32, holding lower encoder layers ![][image123] completely frozen and executing spectral causal closure exclusively across the upper reader layers ![][image124] \[Hypothesis\]. At online assembly time, for ![][image125] chunks ordered as ![][image126], causal masking guarantees that chunk ![][image127] only attends to chunk ![][image128] for ![][image129]5 \[Verified Fact\]. Consequently, the ![][image125]\-chunk subspace coupling operator ![][image130] is **strictly block-lower-triangular** (![][image131] for ![][image132], so ![][image133]) \[Verified Fact\]. The exact intra-layer and cross-layer causal resolvent ![][image134] therefore terminates finitely and can be evaluated via a ![][image135]\-step Neumann series (![][image136]) or forward block-substitution sweep2 \[Technical Inference\]:

Once the subspace KV shifts ![][image138] are solved in ![][image139] time inside GPU SRAM, a single fused kernel lifts them back to the full ![][image58]\-token cache via ![][image140] and simultaneously applies the exact RoPE ![][image3]\-rotation ![][image141] as the KV pages stream into HBM \[Hypothesis\].

## **5\. System Architecture: Components, Data Structures, and Execution Flow**

ResolventKV is architected as a modular runtime layer situated between a disaggregated KV cache storage engine (such as LMCache or Mooncake46) and the GPU inference scheduler's block manager (SGLang's RadixAttention or vLLM's PagedAttention8). The architecture decouples heavy token-level prefill from lightweight spectral causal closure across three operational stages: Offline Chunk Ingestion, Provenance-Bound Content-Addressed Storage, and Online Subspace Resolvent Assembly.  
![][image159]

### **Architectural Components and End-to-End Execution Flow**

When an incoming request arrives at the serving engine, it first passes through standard exact-prefix matching in SGLang's RadixCache8 \[Verified Fact\]. To prevent sequence-start attention sinks from corrupting downstream positional rotations, ResolventKV enforces Irminsul's **First-Chunk Carve-Out (![][image145])**7: the initial ![][image160]\-token system preamble is pinned at offset ![][image16] and always served via exact prefix matching, because empirical measurements confirm that attention sink ratios collapse to their stationary floor (![][image161] on MLA and ![][image162] on GQA) for all chunks starting at ![][image163]8 \[Verified Fact\]. Any unmatched prompt tail is segmented by a **Marker-Pinned Content-Defined Chunker (CDC)** that applies a single-pass Gear rolling hash aligned to structural prompt boundaries (such as document delimiters or tool-call blocks, defaulting to ![][image164] tokens) and fingerprints each segment with xxHash647 \[Verified Fact\].  
To prevent the provenance-blind cache collisions uncovered in September 2026 across vLLM, LMCache, and Mooncake—where content-addressed stores hash only token IDs and silently return foreign KV states computed under incompatible LoRA adapters, weight versions, or quantization precisions46—ResolventKV's **Provenance-Bound Key Generator** enforces **KV Provenance Contract ![][image165]**47 \[Verified Fact\]. Every cache lookup derives its key via a cryptographic digest binding the token fingerprint to all five computational and isolation dimensions46 \[Technical Inference\]:  
![][image166]  
If a chunk triggers a cache miss, it is encoded under the canonical ![][image160]\-token sink prefix ![][image98]. Following the functional depth split of CoMem and EncBank32, lower layers ![][image123] store their position-free KV slices (or compact residuals), while for each upper reader layer ![][image124], the **Offline Spiked-Subspace Extractor (SubspacePacker)** captures the native FlashAttention log-sum-exp vector ![][image167], executes batched optimal singular value shrinkage (eOptShrink1) to isolate the top\-![][image118] left singular basis ![][image116], and runs a batched JVP pass over those ![][image118] modes to extract the low-rank factored Frechet susceptibility tensors ![][image120] \[Hypothesis\].  
Upon a cache hit for ![][image125] chunks assembled in target order ![][image126], the **Online Subspace Resolvent Engine (ResolventStitcher)** executes inside a dedicated CUDA Green Context51 concurrently with host-to-device PCIe/RDMA DMA transfers29 \[Technical Inference\]. The runtime fetches the compact **Spectral Causal Summary Packets (SCSPs)** first, solves the block-lower-triangular Neumann resolvent sweep across layers ![][image168] inside GPU SRAM, and applies a fused scatter-add and RoPE ![][image3]\-rotation kernel (fused\_scatter\_lift\_and\_rotate) as the bulk KV pages land in GPU HBM, immediately prior to prefilling the active user query ![][image59] \[Hypothesis\].

### **Failure Modes and Runtime Safeguards**

Two primary operational failure modes are guarded by deterministic runtime checks. First, an **Out-of-Linear-Regime Perturbation** occurs when a downstream chunk ![][image57] is so heavily conditioned on an upstream chunk ![][image201] (such as a chunk composed primarily of unresolved pronouns referring to entities in ![][image201]) that the cross-chunk attention mass capture ratio ![][image202] exceeds the radius within which first-order Frechet linearization of the SwiGLU MLP remains accurate \[Hypothesis\]. To guard against this, ResolventStitcher checks the mean capture gate ![][image203] at the first upper layer (requiring ![][image204]); if ![][image205] (default ![][image206]), the runtime aborts the linear sweep for chunk ![][image57] and seamlessly triggers SAFE-KV causal suffix forwarding5 or EncBank upper-layer continuation32 \[Proposed Experiment\]. Second, **Spiked-Rank Underflow** occurs on high-entropy non-natural text (such as dense random hex dumps) where the empirical singular value spectrum lacks a dominant spike above the BBP threshold ![][image47]1. During offline ingestion, if the top\-![][image118] singular values capture less than ![][image207] of the centered Frobenius energy, the chunk is tagged UNCOMPRESSIBLE\_RAW and bypassed by PIC \[Technical Inference\].

## **6\. Algorithm Specification and Mathematical Complexity**

### **Mathematical Formulation of the Subspace Resolvent Sweep**

Given ![][image125] cached chunks ![][image67] placed at target global token offsets ![][image208] after the ![][image160]\-token sink prefix ![][image98], let ![][image209] denote the positional shift of chunk ![][image210]7. At each upper layer ![][image211], each chunk ![][image212] holds isolated spectral centroids ![][image213] and accumulated current-layer subspace KV perturbations ![][image214] (initialized to zero at ![][image215]).  
First, the algorithm forms the position-corrected effective centroids by adding the current-layer subspace perturbations and applying the closed-form RoPE rotation ![][image216]7:  
![][image217]  
Second, for every causal chunk pair ![][image218] (![][image219]), the algorithm evaluates the ![][image220] cross-chunk spectral attention logits shifted by the effective log-multiplicity ![][image221] of mode ![][image222]:  
![][image223]  
From these logits, the cross-chunk log-normalizer ![][image224] and the cross-chunk value aggregation ![][image225] are computed. Third, the log-partition convex gating matrix ![][image226] weights the direct cross-chunk shift ![][image227], and a ![][image228]\-step Neumann resolvent refinement2 closes transitive intra-layer routing across the strictly block-lower-triangular system:  
![][image229]  
Fourth, the closed attention shift propagates to layer ![][image230] through the precomputed low-rank Frechet susceptibility operators ![][image120] with residual persistence ![][image231]:  
![][image232]  
Finally, a fused landing kernel lifts ![][image233] back to the ![][image58]\-token cache via ![][image117] and applies ![][image216] in place.

### **Executable-Grade Pseudocode**

Python  
import torch  
import torch.nn.functional as F

def offline\_extract\_scsp(  
    K\_iso: torch.Tensor,      \# \[H\_kv, c, d\_h\] un-rotated isolated Keys at layer l  
    V\_iso: torch.Tensor,      \# \[H\_kv, c, d\_h\] isolated Values at layer l  
    Q\_iso: torch.Tensor,      \# \[H\_kv, c, d\_h\] GQA-grouped isolated Queries at layer l  
    LSE\_iso: torch.Tensor,    \# \[H\_kv, c\] group-averaged FlashAttention log-sum-exp  
    layer\_jvp\_fn: callable,   \# Function computing (dK\_{l+1}, dV\_{l+1}) for a basis perturbation dO\_l  
    r: int \= 8  
) \-\> dict:  
    """  
    Offline Stage 1: Extracts the Spectral Causal Summary Packet (SCSP) for a single chunk at layer l.  
    Uses Optimal Shrinkage SVD (eOptShrinkQ principle) on concatenated KV variations.  
    """  
    H\_kv, c, d\_h \= K\_iso.shape  
    KV\_cat \= torch.cat(\[K\_iso \- K\_iso.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True),  
                        V\_iso \- V\_iso.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)\], dim=-1) \# \[H\_kv, c, 2\*d\_h\]  
      
    U, S, \_ \= torch.linalg.svd(KV\_cat.float(), full\_matrices=False)  
    U\_r \= U\[:, :, :r\].to(K\_iso.dtype) \# \[H\_kv, c, r\], orthonormal columns  
      
    U\_sq \= U\_r \*\* 2  
    Q\_tilde \= torch.einsum("hcr,hcd-\>hrd", U\_r, Q\_iso)  
    K\_tilde \= torch.einsum("hcr,hcd-\>hrd", U\_r, K\_iso)  
    V\_tilde \= torch.einsum("hcr,hcd-\>hrd", U\_r, V\_iso)  
    LSE\_tilde \= torch.einsum("hcr,hc-\>hr", U\_sq, LSE\_iso)  
      
    L\_K\_tilde \= torch.log(U\_sq.sum(dim=1).clamp(min\=1e-6)) \# \[H\_kv, r\]  
    J\_K, J\_V \= layer\_jvp\_fn(U\_r) \# Factored as \[H\_kv, r, d\_h, r\_proj\] and \[H\_kv, r, r\_proj, d\_h\]  
      
    return {  
        "U\_r": U\_r, "Q\_tilde": Q\_tilde, "K\_tilde": K\_tilde, "V\_tilde": V\_tilde,  
        "LSE\_tilde": LSE\_tilde, "L\_K\_tilde": L\_K\_tilde, "J\_K": J\_K, "J\_V": J\_V  
    }

def online\_resolvent\_causal\_sweep(  
    packets: list\[list\[dict\]\], \# \[L\_upper\]\[m\] list of SCSP dicts for m assembled chunks  
    target\_offsets: list\[int\], \# \[m\] global token start positions p\_1 ... p\_m  
    source\_offsets: list\[int\], \# \[m\] canonical source positions p\_{1,src} ... p\_{m,src}  
    rope\_rotate\_fn: callable,  \# Closed-form RoPE delta-rotation R(delta)  
    tau\_linear: float \= 0.42,  \# Linear regime safeguard threshold  
    alpha\_res: float \= 0.90    \# Residual persistence factor across layers  
) \-\> tuple\[list\[list\[tuple\[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor\]\]\], bool\]:  
    """  
    Online Stage 3: Executes the Block-Lower-Triangular Subspace Resolvent Sweep across L\_upper layers.  
    Returns per-layer, per-chunk rank-r KV updates (dK\_tilde, dV\_tilde) and a fallback flag.  
    """  
    L\_upper \= len(packets)  
    m \= len(packets\[0\])  
    H\_kv, r, d\_h \= packets\[0\]\[0\]\["K\_tilde"\].shape  
    device \= packets\[0\]\[0\]\["K\_tilde"\].device  
    dtype \= packets\[0\]\[0\]\["K\_tilde"\].dtype  
      
    dK\_curr \= \[torch.zeros((H\_kv, r, d\_h), device=device, dtype=dtype) for \_ in range(m)\]  
    dV\_curr \= \[torch.zeros((H\_kv, r, d\_h), device=device, dtype=dtype) for \_ in range(m)\]  
    all\_layer\_updates \= \[\]  
      
    deltas \= \[p\_tgt \- p\_src for p\_tgt, p\_src in zip(target\_offsets, source\_offsets)\]  
      
    for l in range(L\_upper):  
        layer\_pkts \= packets\[l\]  
        Q\_hat, K\_hat, V\_hat \= \[\], \[\], \[\]  
          
        for i in range(m):  
            pkt \= layer\_pkts\[i\]  
            k\_eff \= pkt\["K\_tilde"\] \+ dK\_curr\[i\]  
            v\_eff \= pkt\["V\_tilde"\] \+ dV\_curr\[i\]  
            Q\_hat.append(rope\_rotate\_fn(pkt\["Q\_tilde"\], deltas\[i\]))  
            K\_hat.append(rope\_rotate\_fn(k\_eff, deltas\[i\]))  
            V\_hat.append(v\_eff)  
              
        all\_layer\_updates.append(\[(dK\_curr\[i\], dV\_curr\[i\]) for i in range(m)\])  
          
        dO\_closed \= \[torch.zeros((H\_kv, r, d\_h), device=device, dtype=dtype) for \_ in range(m)\]  
          
        for i in range(1, m):  
            pkt\_i \= layer\_pkts\[i\]  
            K\_prev \= torch.cat(K\_hat\[:i\], dim=1)  
            V\_prev \= torch.cat(V\_hat\[:i\], dim=1)  
            dO\_prev \= torch.cat(dO\_closed\[:i\], dim=1)  
            L\_K\_prev \= torch.cat(\[layer\_pkts\[b\]\["L\_K\_tilde"\] for b in range(i)\], dim=1)  
              
            logits \= torch.einsum("hrd,hkd-\>hrk", Q\_hat\[i\], K\_prev) / (d\_h \*\* 0.5)  
            logits \= logits \+ L\_K\_prev.unsqueeze(1)  
              
            LSE\_cross \= torch.logsumexp(logits.float(), dim=-1).to(dtype)  
            attn\_cross \= F.softmax(logits.float(), dim=-1).to(dtype)  
              
            gamma\_i \= torch.sigmoid((LSE\_cross \- pkt\_i\["LSE\_tilde"\]).float()).to(dtype)  
              
            if l \== 0 and gamma\_i.mean().item() \> tau\_linear:  
                return \[\], True  
                  
            O\_cross \= torch.einsum("hrk,hkd-\>hrd", attn\_cross, V\_prev)  
            O\_iso\_approx \= pkt\_i\["V\_tilde"\]  
              
            dO\_1 \= gamma\_i.unsqueeze(-1) \* (O\_cross \- O\_iso\_approx)  
            dO\_2 \= gamma\_i.unsqueeze(-1) \* torch.einsum("hrk,hkd-\>hrd", attn\_cross, dO\_prev)  
            dO\_closed\[i\] \= dO\_1 \+ dO\_2  
              
        if l \< L\_upper \- 1:  
            dK\_next, dV\_next \= \[\], \[\]  
            for i in range(m):  
                pkt\_i \= layer\_pkts\[i\]  
                J\_K\_A, J\_K\_B \= pkt\_i\["J\_K"\]  
                J\_V\_A, J\_V\_B \= pkt\_i\["J\_V"\]  
                  
                step\_K \= torch.einsum("hrdp,hrpe,hre-\>hrd", J\_K\_A, J\_K\_B, dO\_closed\[i\])  
                step\_V \= torch.einsum("hrdp,hrpe,hre-\>hrd", J\_V\_A, J\_V\_B, dO\_closed\[i\])  
                  
                dK\_next.append(alpha\_res \* dK\_curr\[i\] \+ step\_K)  
                dV\_next.append(alpha\_res \* dV\_curr\[i\] \+ step\_V)  
            dK\_curr, dV\_curr \= dK\_next, dV\_next  
              
    return all\_layer\_updates, False

def fused\_scatter\_lift\_and\_rotate(  
    K\_iso: torch.Tensor,       \# \[H\_kv, c, d\_h\]  
    V\_iso: torch.Tensor,       \# \[H\_kv, c, d\_h\]  
    U\_r: torch.Tensor,         \# \[H\_kv, c, r\]  
    dK\_tilde: torch.Tensor,    \# \[H\_kv, r, d\_h\]  
    dV\_tilde: torch.Tensor,    \# \[H\_kv, r, d\_h\]  
    delta\_pos: int,  
    rope\_rotate\_fn: callable  
) \-\> tuple\[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor\]:  
    """  
    Fused HBM landing kernel: lifts rank-r causal shift to c tokens and applies RoPE delta-rotation.  
    """  
    K\_updated \= K\_iso \+ torch.einsum("hcr,hrd-\>hcd", U\_r, dK\_tilde)  
    V\_updated \= V\_iso \+ torch.einsum("hcr,hrd-\>hcd", U\_r, dV\_tilde)  
    return rope\_rotate\_fn(K\_updated, delta\_pos), V\_updated

### **Edge Cases and Theoretical Limitations**

Three structural edge cases govern the behavior of the algorithm. First, as demonstrated in Irminsul's ROC and attention-sink studies across MLA, GQA, and MHA8, chunks originally encoded at position ![][image145] accumulate extreme attention-sink norms that fail when shifted into the prompt interior, whereas every chunk encoded at ![][image163] collapses to the stationary sink baseline (![][image161] on MLA vs. ![][image262] at ![][image263]; ![][image162] on GQA vs. ![][image264] at ![][image263])8 \[Verified Fact\]. Note that MHA remains elevated at ![][image265] through ![][image266]8 \[Verified Fact\]; thus, ResolventKV restricts zero-recompute guarantees to GQA and MLA models and always precomputes chunks at canonical offset ![][image180] after the pinned ![][image160]\-token system preamble \[Technical Inference\]. Second, when an identical chunk appears multiple times in the same prompt at distinct positions ![][image267], both instances read the same immutable SCSP from the cache registry, but ResolventStitcher materializes separate copy-on-write HBM pages45 because instance ![][image222] receives non-zero causal perturbation from instance ![][image268] \[Technical Inference\]. Third, the fundamental theoretical limitation of ResolventKV is that cross-chunk state modification between any pair of chunks ![][image269] is bottlenecked through rank ![][image118] (![][image270]) \[Technical Inference\]. While the final user query ![][image59] still attends to the full ![][image58]\-token resolution of every chunk ![][image57], indirect chunk-to-chunk conditioning cannot transmit more than ![][image118] orthogonal feature shifts per KV head simultaneously \[Technical Inference\].

## **7\. Critical Falsifiable Experiment**

Designing a rigorous, falsifiable experiment for KV cache reuse requires controlling for two major methodological confounders identified in late 2026 literature. First, an August 2026 audit of latent cache relays (**Native Relay**, arXiv:2608.04893) uncovered **Receiver-Necessity Dissociation**: on standard natural benchmarks (such as GSM8K, ARC-Challenge, and MedQA) where the receiver LLM can solve the problem using its parametric weights or the query alone, cache-sharing interventions read zero effect within a Holm-corrected equivalence margin of ![][image10] percentage points23 \[Verified Fact\]. Conversely, in a calibrated receiver-necessity regime using ![][image271] procedurally generated sender-private facts that the receiver cannot reconstruct without reading the cache, aligned cache state reaches ceiling accuracy (![][image272] to ![][image21]) across five model checkpoints (Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, Mistral-Nemo-12B, and phi-4), whereas matched answer-irrelevant intact caches drop to ![][image273]–![][image274] (a True-minus-Intact contrast of ![][image275] to ![][image276] points) and mismatched deranged caches or zeroed relays collapse23 \[Verified Fact\]. Second, **CoMem** and **EncBank** (October 2026\) demonstrated that on Qwen3-8B, splitting the decoder at layer ![][image50] reduces persistent memory from ![][image200] (full-depth 16-bit KV) to ![][image277] in BF16 (an ![][image278] reduction, or ![][image279] for ![][image280] tokens) and ![][image281] in 4-bit H4 (![][image282] of H16's store, holding RULER accuracy at ![][image283] vs. ![][image284] for H16), while upper-layer adaptation lifts 1,986-item LoCoMo accuracy from ![][image285] to ![][image286]32 \[Verified Fact\].

### **Experimental Protocol, Metrics, and Falsification Threshold**

The critical experiment tests the hypothesis that on multi-hop RAG and agentic workloads with ![][image299] assembled chunks (![][image114] tokens each, ![][image254] context tokens total), **ResolventKV** (![][image300]) will achieve ![][image301] **Normalized Answer Preservation** relative to exact full prefill (compared to ![][image29]–![][image28] for un-repaired prefix-conditioned composition12) while reducing online repair FLOPs by ![][image302] and delivering a ![][image303] **to ![][image304] end-to-end TTFT speedup** on a single GPU \[Proposed Experiment\].  
The minimal prototype consists of a 1,200-line Python/PyTorch and Triton extension hooking into SGLang's RadixCache across three open-weight models spanning GQA and MLA architectures: Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (the exact model used in SAFE-KV12), Qwen/Qwen3-8B (used in EncBank32 and Native Relay23), and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite (16B/2.4B native MLA-MoE used in Irminsul8) \[Proposed Experiment\]. The reproducible dataset suite comprises **HotpotQA-500** and **2WikiMultihopQA-500** (![][image299] documents per query from SAFE-KV12), **MuSiQue** (multi-step reasoning chains where KV Packet and single-hop PIC degrade6), **SRA-Bench** and **Toolathlon** (agentic tool-use trajectories from ATTUNER and Irminsul6), and the **Calibrated Receiver-Necessity Suite** (500 sender-private multi-hop facts23) \[Proposed Experiment\].  
All runs execute on two hardware tiers: Tier 1 uses a single **NVIDIA L40S (48 GB GDDR6)** with PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128 on Ubuntu 24.04 (matching SAFE-KV's exact latency testbed27), and Tier 2 uses a single **NVIDIA H200 (141 GB HBM3e)** with PCIe Gen5 host DRAM offload (matching Irminsul's testbed26) \[Proposed Experiment\]. Six baselines are compared under KVShareArena's controlled protocol9: (1) **Full Prefill** (behavioral reference), (2) **Naive Prefix-Conditioned PIC \+ RoPE ![][image3]\-Rotation** (![][image68]5 / Irminsul7), (3) **CacheBlend** (![][image305] token recomputation in LMCache11), (4) **KV Packet** (![][image306] soft-token wrappers41), (5) **ATTUNER** (query-side ![][image143] LoRA6), and (6) **SAFE-KV** (Risk-Guided K2 actual suffix forwarding5) \[Proposed Experiment\].  
Four primary metrics govern evaluation: (1) **Normalized Answer Preservation** ![][image307] under greedy 16-token decoding5, (2) **First-Answer-Token KL Divergence** ![][image308]5, (3) **Gold EM/F1** and **True-minus-Intact (![][image290]) Calibrated Contrast**5, and (4) **End-to-End TTFT (ms)** including DMA transfer, resolvent sweep, scatter lift, and query prefill27 \[Proposed Experiment\]. The experiment succeeds if ResolventKV achieves ![][image309] Answer Preservation and ![][image310] on HotpotQA-500 and 2Wiki-500 at ![][image299] chunks while keeping TTFT below ![][image311] of Full Prefill on the NVIDIA L40S \[Proposed Experiment\]. Conversely, the hypothesis is **falsified** if non-linearities in the upper-layer SwiGLU MLPs cause first-order Frechet susceptibility ![][image312] to accumulate drift such that Answer Preservation on 2Wiki-500 falls below ![][image313] at rank ![][image314], or requires triggering the ![][image315] suffix-recomputation fallback on more than ![][image274] of requests \[Proposed Experiment\].

## **8\. Technology Stack and Systems Rationale**

The ResolventKV software stack is selected strictly for hardware-level execution mechanics rather than ecosystem convention. The serving engine substrate builds on **SGLang (RadixAttention)** rather than vanilla vLLM because SGLang's radix tree natively supports variable-length prefix subtrees and observer-mode fall-through hooks (\_by\_hash), as validated by Irminsul and Leyline7 \[Verified Fact\]. This allows exact prefix hits (including the mandatory ![][image145] attention-sink preamble) to execute along the zero-overhead radix path while routing only the shifted dynamic chunks to ResolventStitcher \[Technical Inference\].  
For the core attention primitives, ResolventKV utilizes **FlashAttention-2** (for GQA models) and **FlashMLA** (for MLA models) configured with native softmax\_lse output enabled7 \[Verified Fact\]. Both kernels already compute the exact row-wise log-sum-exp normalizer ![][image316] in warp registers during online softmax normalization; writing this ![][image317] scalar vector to HBM during offline chunk ingestion adds zero arithmetic overhead and provides the exact partition function required by Pillar 1 \[Technical Inference\].  
The online block-lower-triangular resolvent sweep and the fused U\_r @ dK\_tilde \+ RoPE\_delta landing pass are implemented in **TileLang**51 and **Triton**54 \[Technical Inference\]. Because the entire ![][image125]\-chunk subspace state for a layer (![][image318]) occupies only ![][image319] in bfloat16, TileLang's explicit tile-level shared-memory scheduling keeps the subspace matrices resident in GPU SRAM across the ![][image135]\-step Neumann iteration, avoiding intermediate HBM reads and writes \[Technical Inference\]. To overlap this computation with PCIe Gen5 cache loading, the runtime leverages **CUDA Driver API v13.3 Green Contexts** (torch.cuda.green\_contexts.GreenContext, introduced in mid-202651) to partition a dedicated ![][image320] workqueue for ResolventStitcher while the primary SMs and copy engines stream quantized KV pages from **LMCache**50 \[Technical Inference\].

## **10\. Adoption Strategy and Structural Defensibility**

The immediate initial adopters for ResolventKV are high-concurrency agentic orchestration platforms, autonomous coding assistants, and enterprise multi-hop RAG operators deploying open-weight models (DeepSeek-V3/V4, Qwen3, Llama-3.3/4) on self-managed Kubernetes inference stacks (llm-d, SGLang, vLLM)7 \[Technical Inference\]. As documented in the OpenClaw operational post-mortems7, these engineering teams already experience severe latency and compute regressions whenever retrieval re-ranking or context compaction shifts 40K-token histories off the exact-prefix path \[Verified Fact\].  
To maximize developer adoption while building a defensible commercial product, the deployment strategy separates the technology into an open-source single-node primitive and a commercial distributed state fabric \[Technical Inference\]. The open-source core (Apache-2.0) releases the SCSP tensor specification, the Triton/TileLang ResolventStitcher kernels, an OpenAI /v1/responses compatible server adapter (modeled on KV Packet's drop-in HTTP/SSE interface49), and official submissions to the **KVShareArena** public leaderboard9 \[Technical Inference\]. The commercial tier provides a multi-node, provenance-enforced KV memory fabric that manages asynchronous background SCSP extraction across disaggregated Encode-Prefill-Decode (EPD) clusters57, integrates with Modular-style cache-aware routers51, and enforces multi-tenant cryptographic isolation under Provenance Contract ![][image165]46 \[Technical Inference\].  
Incumbents cannot trivially copy or obviate ResolventKV through larger context windows or brute-force hardware scaling. As context lengths expand from 128K to 2M+ tokens, full-prefill compute scales quadratically ![][image328] while KV cache capacity rapidly outgrows GPU HBM (where a single 128K-token session on a 70B model consumes ![][image329] of BF16 KV cache, leaving room for only three concurrent sessions on a dual-GPU node36) \[Verified Fact\]. Furthermore, as agentic workflows incorporate more modular skills and retrieved documents, the combinatorial permutations of ![][image125] chunks (![][image330]) drive exact-prefix cache hit rates asymptotically toward zero7 \[Technical Inference\]. Achieving ResolventKV's performance requires tight numerical and systems co-design across three layers that resist superficial replication: (1) stabilizing optimal singular value shrinkage (eOptShrink1) and low-rank Frechet susceptibility across diverse attention architectures (GQA, MLA, and hybrid linear-attention models26), (2) fusing low-rank outer-product lifting with RoPE ![][image3]\-rotation inside custom warp-level GPU kernels during DMA landing, and (3) calibrating the ![][image315] causal-fallback gate to guarantee strict behavioral equivalence under latency SLOs5 \[Technical Inference\].

## **11\. Adversarial Failure Analysis and Kill Criteria**

An adversarial review of ResolventKV identifies two primary technical vulnerabilities, estimates the probability of concurrent prior art, establishes controls against false-positive benchmark gains, and defines hard kill criteria.  
The strongest technical objection is that **non-linearities in deep SwiGLU MLPs and RMSNorm layers could break the first-order Frechet susceptibility approximation (![][image312]) across stacked upper layers** \[Hypothesis\]. Pillar 2 assumes that mapping a layer\-![][image84] attention shift ![][image193] to the layer\-![][image194] KV shift ![][image122] via a linear Jacobian evaluated around the isolated chunk trajectory ![][image66] remains accurate across ![][image171] layers. If the gated non-linearity ![][image331] induces high second-order curvature when cross-chunk attention shifts are large, Taylor truncation errors could compound across layers \[Hypothesis\]. Two empirical facts mitigate this risk: first, **ATTUNER** (September 2026\) proved that holding cached ![][image332] states completely un-updated (![][image333]) while correcting only the attention routing scores already recovers nearly all multi-artifact accuracy6 \[Verified Fact\], proving that the deep value manifold is highly resilient to moderate routing perturbations; second, if cross-layer JVP error compounds over 20 layers, ResolventKV can restrict JVP propagation to a 2-layer local horizon while applying exact log-partition stitching (Pillar 1\) at every layer \[Hypothesis\].  
A second objection is the **hidden offline write-amplification cost**: extracting the rank\-![][image118] SVD basis and batched JVP susceptibility during chunk ingestion adds approximately ![][image334] to ![][image335] the compute of a single isolated chunk prefill \[Technical Inference\]. As **EncBank** demonstrated in October 2026, end-to-end caching gains depend critically on preparation costs and reuse frequency58 \[Verified Fact\]. If a transient tool output is only used once, offline SCSP extraction wastes GPU cycles \[Technical Inference\]. ResolventKV mitigates this via **lazy promotion** in RadixCache: chunks are initially stored as standard prefix-conditioned KV on their first pass, and SubspacePacker is only triggered asynchronously when a chunk's content hash registers a second lookup at a shifted position (![][image336]) \[Technical Inference\].  
The estimated probability that unpublished concurrent work inside a major AI lab already solves this exact mechanism is ![][image337] **to ![][image311]** \[Speculation\]. Between April and October 2026, ten independent groups published papers on non-prefix KV reuse9, and industrial labs such as DeepSeek-AI (which released *DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the limits of KV cache compression* in 202656) are actively co-designing low-rank KV compression with serving kernels \[Verified Fact\]. Furthermore, any apparent benchmark gains in early prototypes must be audited against two alternative explanations: (a) **Receiver-Necessity Dissociation**23, where models score high on natural benchmarks without actually reading the repaired cache (controlled by testing on the 500-item Calibrated Receiver-Necessity suite23), and (b) **Position-Only Recovery**, where simple RoPE ![][image3]\-rotation accounts for the gain on single-artifact tasks (controlled by benchmarking strictly against the position-aligned prefix-conditioned baseline ![][image68]5) \[Verified Fact\].  
The project is governed by three **Hard Kill Criteria**: (1) **Fidelity Kill**—if at rank ![][image338], Normalized Answer Preservation on 2WikiMultihopQA-500 (![][image299] documents) fails to exceed ![][image339] without triggering token-level suffix recomputation on ![][image340] of queries; (2) **Latency Kill**—if the combined wall-clock execution time of the online subspace resolvent sweep and fused scatter lift exceeds ![][image337] of Full Prefill time on an NVIDIA L40S for an 8,192-token context; and (3) **Storage Kill**—if achieving ![][image341] Answer Preservation requires storing unfactored susceptibility tensors that exceed ![][image274] of the base KV cache footprint \[Proposed Experiment\].

### **Statement of Search and Access Limitations**

To maintain strict evidentiary transparency, two access boundaries encountered during primary source verification are noted. First, while one direct crawler request to the full HTML body of https\://arxiv.org/html/2610.15186v1 (SAFE-KV) returned an access block5, its complete abstract, exact quantitative results (![][image343] baseline preservation, ![][image344] donor-copy recovery, ![][image345] actual suffix forwarding, and ![][image346] context re-encoding ratios at K2), methodology (Sections 4.1 and 4.2), and hardware specifications (NVIDIA L40S, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128) were verified across multiple indexed excerpts and figure/table records5. Second, internal proprietary caching architectures inside closed commercial APIs (such as OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google Gemini) and unpublished patent filings within their 18-month confidentiality window could not be inspected.

### **Decisive Recommendation**

**Investigate One Specific Mathematical Unknown First (72-Hour Diagnostic Gate), Then Build the PoC.**  
Before investing engineering weeks into custom Triton/TileLang kernels or SGLang RadixCache integration, the team must execute a **72-hour offline PyTorch diagnostic experiment** on a single NVIDIA L40S GPU using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on the 100-item 2Wiki-100 benchmark slice from SAFE-KV27 \[Proposed Experiment\]. This diagnostic isolates the single highest-risk mathematical unknown: **whether first-order Frechet susceptibility (![][image312]) across upper layers ![][image347] remains within the linear convergence basin without triggering SwiGLU phase drift** \[Hypothesis\]. Specifically, the diagnostic will compare **Arm A** (Pillar 1 Only: Exact Log-Partition Routing Adjustment over Frozen Isolated Values), **Arm B** (Pillars 1 \+ 2 \+ 3: Full Subspace Resolvent KV Update at rank ![][image113]), and **Arm C** (SAFE-KV Donor-Copy Suffix Oracle) \[Proposed Experiment\]. If Arm B lifts 2Wiki-100 Normalized Answer Preservation from the ![][image33] naive baseline (and ![][image34] document-only repair baseline27) to ![][image348], the team should proceed immediately to Phase 2 and build the full SGLang/Triton runtime PoC. If multi-layer MLP non-linearity caps Arm B below ![][image313], the team should restrict JVP propagation to the final four upper layers where value-routing sensitivity peaks34 or terminate the training-free JVP propagation path.
